description: A subscript that is not one of the COBOL-85 forms — integer-1 ("may be signed and, if signed, it must be positive", §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR6), data-name-2 or index-name-1, each optionally followed by + or - an unsigned nonzero integer (§1985:III.2), where data-name-2 "must be a numeric elementary item representing an integer" (SR5) — a COBOL-2002 relaxation of a COBOL-85 restriction, QUOTED from ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex F.2 item 133: "Subscripting with arithmetic expressions. An arithmetic expression may now be used as a subscript, not just the forms data-name + integer and data-name - integer." So 1.5, -1, 0, I + 0 and a data-name of PIC 9V9 are each the 2002 arithmetic-expression form (kb/Work PB5074). COBOL-85 is the edition a 2002 Annex F.2 'formerly' statement describes: the owner's decision of 2026-10-31 (kb/Work PB4305) makes the F.2 statements the rule for the 85 edge, as D-SIGN2 (item 124) and PB3683 (item 123) did; GnuCOBOL -std=cobol85 accepts some of them as dialect leniency, which rule 1 places below the ISO text. The shape is gated in VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitSubscriptPart, once per subscript, and the data-name's description in SubscriptBinder.ScreenCobol85SubscriptDataNames, where the item is known (kb/Work PB4305, PB5074; VCR row 7.47).
display: a subscript that is not a COBOL-85 positive integer, integer data-name or index-name, each optionally followed by + or - an unsigned nonzero integer
vcr: VCR Table 7 row 7.47 - the 2002 Annex F.2 relaxations of COBOL-85 restrictions (item 133)
